families.name: quasi-Riemann hypothesis
families.paper_claim: All Dirichlet L-functions and finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(sqrt(-3)) are zero-free for Re(s)>7/8, allowing the principal pole at s=1; in particular zeta is zero-free there.
families.formal_scope_documented: Zeta, all Dirichlet characters at positive moduli, and finite-order Hecke characters over Q(sqrt(-3)); principal-character point s=1 omitted. A linked formal scope also gives a nonexplicit uniform c/log(q) gap for real zeros of primitive nonprincipal real characters q>=3, both parities; it does not exclude all zeros in (0,1). Later paper applications are excluded.
families.known_gap: Paper-to-formalization correspondence and mathematical proof not independently audited here; no Comparator replay. Later applications and explicit Siegel-zero constant are out of scope.
families.next_check: Replay only the four named configs in a trusted environment, then do a theorem-by-theorem source-to-challenge review.

families.name: direct finiteness and related group-algebra claims
families.paper_claim: Current family headline includes an October 4 claim of a finitely presented torsion-free group with a direct-finiteness counterexample over F_2 and a finite 2-dimensional classifying complex.
families.formal_scope_documented: Older characteristic-two formal target constructs a finitely presented group with an odd-prime-order element, so it is torsionful; nonsoficity is outside formal statements. Separate formal targets cover a determinant counterexample (without the paper's spectral-measure integral formulation) and an odd-characteristic counterexample with torsion.
families.known_gap: The current October 4 torsion-free paper has no matching entry in lean/docs/197.md or formalization.yaml, and its torsion-free requirement is incompatible with the selected older theorem's odd-prime torsion witness.
families.next_check: Encode and prove the October 4 torsion-free theorem itself, including the group and finite 2-complex claims; do not reuse the torsionful challenge as coverage.

families.name: threshold parallel repetition for entangled games
families.paper_claim: Universal exponential rate proportional to delta^5/(1+log(|A||B|)); separate fixed-question-distribution cubic rate.
families.formal_scope_documented: Arbitrary correlated questions, every finite-dimensional joint strategy and supremum, with a universal delta^13/(1+log(|A||B|)) rate; no attainment assumption. Cubic rate is out of scope.
families.known_gap: Formal target proves a weaker exponent than paper's stated universal quantitative bound. Since 0<delta<1, delta^13 gives a weaker estimate than delta^5.
families.next_check: Either keep delta^13 as the stated formal scope or create/replay separate delta^5 and fixed-distribution cubic challenges.

families.name: free group factor isomorphism
families.paper_claim: L(F_2) is normally trace-preservingly isomorphic to L(F_3); the paper derives all interpolated factor isomorphisms and fundamental group R_{>0}.
families.formal_scope_documented: A standalone Comparator challenge targets normal trace-preserving equivalence of all formalized interpolated factors r,s>1, including infinity. The fundamental-group statement is not the selected Comparator target.
families.known_gap: The config and Lean theorem exist, but formalization.yaml has no free-group-factor, InterpolatedFactors, or allInterpolatedIsomorphic record. No replay or independent definition-level match against standard L(F_r) objects was completed.
families.next_check: Audit the challenge's group-von-Neumann/corner/trace/topology definitions against the paper, register the result in the catalogue, and run only InterpolatedFactors.json.
